purpose: Almotriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults and teenagers. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with a migraine. It is not used to prevent migraines, only to treat them once they start.
how_it_works: When you get a migraine, certain blood vessels in your brain widen and cause pain. Almotriptan works by attaching to specific receptors in your brain that cause those blood vessels to narrow back to their normal size. It also helps block pain signals from being sent to your brain, which is why it helps stop the migraine.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, dry mouth, dizziness, and a warm or tingling feeling in the body. Some people may also feel tired, drowsy, or have a mild headache after taking it. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have heart disease, history of stroke, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or certain types of migraine called hemiplegic or basilar migraine. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially antidepressants, because dangerous interactions are possible. Seek emergency help right away if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden severe headache after taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 6.25 mg or 12.5 mg taken by mouth at the start of a migraine. If your headache comes back after feeling better, you can take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first one. Do not take more than 2 doses in any 24-hour period.
